slices.focus: Ayaka's disruption-log evidence convinces the section chief to approve a limited pilot of color-coded weather notices and an essential-cargo staging checklist.
slices.summary: Ayaka presents a month of screenshots, clipped printouts, and annotated cargo sheets to the section chief, who approves a limited pilot for weather-affected island sailings. She pairs color-coded notice templates with a small essential-cargo staging checklist, keeping scope narrow to avoid overreach. Sakurai warns that aging equipment limits what any paper process can achieve.
open_loops: Pilot success is not guaranteed — first rough-weather day could collapse it
Aging weather boards and lane markings constrain the design
Staff may resist new templates as extra overhead
decisions: Ayaka's self-started disruption log led to approval for a limited pilot of color-coded bad-weather notices and an essent
